title: Session
description: <root>/<session>/session.json. A session is a working context: a cwd, the part of the catalogs it may use, and the active profile. It holds no model, tool or MCP definitions.

name.description: Display name of the session. Defaults to the folder name.

cwd.description: Working directory of every run in this session. Absolute path (or ~). Beats settings.cwd of this file and the root defaults; a profile's settings.cwd beats it.

category.description: Optional folder name used to group sessions in listings. It does not change the session id.

scope.description: What this session may use. Only profiles are scoped: models, toolsets and MCP servers are always all available, and a profile narrows models itself.

profiles.description: Narrows the profiles. Items: "<category>" for a whole folder, "<category>/<name>" for one file, or "*". A missing key offers every profile; [] offers none. An item that matches no profile is a load error.

active_profile.description: Profile used when a request names none, written <category>/<name>, for example "dev/coder". Must be inside scope.profiles.

model_defaults.description: The model this session uses for each profile, written by the model-default route. Keys are profile IDs (<category>/<name>), values model IDs (<category>/<name>). A profile file is shared by every session, so a session never edits it; this wins over the profile's own model_default.

settings.description: Overrides of the setting keys listed in propertyNames. Objects merge key by key with the level above; arrays and scalars replace it. Each value follows the same key in setting.schema.json.

cwd.description: Working directory of runs. Absolute path (or ~). Defaults, session and profile may all set it; the nearer level wins (profile, then session, then root defaults). The session's top-level cwd beats its settings.cwd.

env_file.description: Dotenv file for the toolset's bash, process and exec when they name no env_file of their own. A relative path is relative to the folder of the root setting.json. Defaults, session and profile may all set it; the nearer level wins. A tool the toolset lacks is not added.

tool_storage_dir.description: Folder that holds the tool storage (bash spill, memory, tasks, fetch, processes, sub-agent runs, write/edit backups), as <folder>/<session>/<category>/<name>/tools. A relative path is relative to the session cwd, so the file tools reach it with no extra path rule; the default is .jad/state. An absolute path outside the cwd needs tools.native.read.paths to allow it. The transcript and staging stay in the root state folder. Defaults, session and profile may all set it; the nearer level wins.
